solution: The configuration (cell, program counter) determines everything and the step map is deterministic, so the state graph is a functional graph on at most N*N*L <= 8*10^6 nodes. Walk it with first-visit timestamps until a state repeats, which exposes the rho's cycle, then replay exactly one lap and collect the cells actually entered. That block B repeats forever; if it is empty the robot has stopped moving and the trail is finite, so print 1. Otherwise the tail is B repeated, whose minimal period divides |B|, so take p = |B| - failure[|B|] from the KMP prefix function and answer p when p divides |B|, else |B|. O(N^2 * L) time and space.
statement_summary: A robot starts on an empty cell of an N by N grid whose border is solid wall and repeats a program of at most N characters drawn from left, right, up and down, skipping any step that would enter a wall. Its trail records only the cells it enters. Print one if that trail is finite, otherwise the length of its eventual repeating block.
notes: The easy-to-miss step is that the cycle in the state graph gives a period of the trail but not necessarily the minimal one, so the prefix-function reduction is needed; sample 1 (answer 2 from a 4-character program) is exactly that case. Verified against a 20000-step direct simulation on 1500 random grids. Statement contains no sentence addressed to the annotator.
